facts.raw_span: a 2-month history of right upper abdominal pain
without nausea, vomiting, chills, or fever
no history of hepatitis, surgery, or hereditary disease, and no underlying medical conditions
afebrile and oriented
right upper abdominal tenderness without rebound or palpable masses
no hepatosplenomegaly
negative Murphy’s sign and shifting dullness
AFP 2.4 µg/l (normal 0.0–7.0)
CEA 11.6 µg/l (normal 0.0–5.0)
a heterogeneous echoic mass near the gallbladder fossa in the right liver lobe

concepts.why: Elevated CA19-9 levels and a heterogeneous echoic mass near the gallbladder fossa in the right liver lobe suggest intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma.
Right upper abdominal tenderness and negative Murphy’s sign suggest cholecystitis.
Right upper abdominal tenderness and gallbladder wall thickening suggest gallstones.

aliases: enlarged lymph nodes in the liver hilum
concepts.why: Contrast-enhanced CT showing multiple enlarged hepatic hilar lymph nodes suggests a possible malignancy, such as intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma.

rationales.F01: Right upper abdominal pain is a common symptom of intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma.
rationales.F05: Abdominal tenderness is a non-specific symptom that can be associated with various conditions, including cholecystitis and gallstones.
rationales.F09: Elevated CEA levels can be seen in various cancers, including intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma.
rationales.F10: High CA19-9 levels are often associated with intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma.
rationales.F12: A heterogeneous echoic mass near the gallbladder fossa is highly suggestive of intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma.

frontier_selector.rationale: High CA19-9 level and a heterogeneous echoic mass near the gallbladder fossa support intrahepatic cholangiocarcinoma, despite some findings also consistent with cholecystitis.
